types.description:
Narrows a listing to a subset of a library.

Every field is combined with `AND`; an absent field places no constraint.

inputFields.name: kind
inputFields.description:
Keep only items of this kind.

Overrides the default depth, because naming a kind is already a statement about depth:
asking for episodes and getting nothing because episodes have parents would be obtuse.
Under `LEAVES` both hold.

inputFields.description: How deep to look. Defaults to the library's top level.

inputFields.description: Keep only items released in or after this year.

inputFields.description:

inputFields.name: audienceRatingFrom
inputFields.description: Keep only items whose audience rating, on its ten-point scale, is at least this.

inputFields.name: yearTo
inputFields.description: Keep only items released in or before this year.

inputFields.name: contentRating
inputFields.description:
Keep only items with exactly this age-rating label, as the metadata source expresses
it — for example `fr/Tous publics`. Not comparable across countries.

inputFields.name: studioContains
inputFields.description:
Keep only items whose studio contains this text, case-insensitively.

A substring rather than a name, which is what a caller typing "HBO" means and what
the Plex surface does. It cannot use an index — a leading wildcard has nothing to
seek to — so it is applied after the library predicate and its cost is bounded by
the library, not the table.

inputFields.name: titleWordPrefix
inputFields.description:
Keep only items having a word that starts with this text.

Matches the title, the sort title and the original title, with accents folded: `le`
finds both "Le Nouveau Jouet" and "Sans Laisser de Traces". A word prefix rather than
full-text search, because full-text indexing is the least portable feature across
database engines and the engine is meant to stay swappable.

inputFields.name: titleCompletion
inputFields.description:
Keep only items whose title this text completes, as a search field offers while it
is typed into.

The text is one phrase beginning a word of the title, a word beginning after a space:

Case does not count and accents do, so `aime` does not complete "aimé". Only the
title is read, not the sort or original title. Empty text completes nothing.

inputFields.name: frame

2880, height: 1540}}` for 4K.

fields.description:

the library auditable from outside. It is not an input — playback addresses a file by

fields.description:
Where a metadata provider streams the file from, relative to the server that
imported it: the trailers the reference's provider supplied, as
`/services/iva/assets/…`. Null for a file of the library. This server streams none.

fields.name: filename
fields.description:
Last segment of `path`, without its directories.

Derived rather than stored: it is what a caller displays, and deriving it keeps one
source of truth for where the file is. Both separators are honored because a library
scanned on Windows stores `\` while the same server may serve a path scanned on Linux.

fields.name: sizeBytes
fields.description: File size in bytes.

fields.name: durationMs
fields.description: Runtime in milliseconds.

fields.name: contentHash
fields.description:
The SHA-1 the scanner computed over the file's contents, in hex: two copies of one
file share it. Null when the scanner computed none.

fields.name: openSubtitlesHash
fields.description:
The file's `OpenSubtitles` hash, in hex — its size plus the 64-bit sums of its first and
last 64 KiB — which subtitle services find a file by. Null when the scanner computed
none.

fields.name: hasThumbnail
fields.description: Whether the file embeds a cover image.

fields.name: has64BitOffsets
fields.description:
Whether an MP4 file uses 64-bit chunk offsets, which some older players cannot read.
Null for a file that is not MP4.

fields.name: optimizedForStreaming
fields.description:
Whether an MP4 file's index precedes its data, so it plays before it has fully
arrived. Null for a file that is not MP4.

fields.name: packetLength
fields.description: The packet size of an MPEG-TS file in bytes: 188, or 192 for Blu-ray's M2TS.

fields.name: hasChapterTextStream
fields.description: Whether chapter names are carried as a text track.

fields.name: analysis
fields.description:
How much of the file's media the server has read. Until its headers are, the file has
no track inside it, no duration and no description, and its version none either.

fields.name: stated
fields.description:
What the file's container states about itself, as the prober printed it. Empty for a
file the scan did not read.

fields.name: sideStreams
fields.description:
What the file carries besides the tracks that play — cover pictures, data tracks,
attached files — by position.

fields.name: streams
fields.description: The tracks inside this file, plus any sidecar subtitle files.

fields.name: readableAsIs
fields.description:
Whether a player reads this file as it is, so that `startStream` can send it untouched
with `directPlay`: one of the formats the player declares holds the file's container (a
Matroska file of nothing but `WebM`'s codecs is held as `webm` too), its video codec and
the codec of the audio track it would play — `audioTrack`, or the
caller's — and the version weighs no more than `maxBitrate`. An empty list in a format
admits anything; names are compared without regard to case. False for a file whose
headers are not read yet (`analysis`): nothing known of it says a player reads it.

fields.description: Whether the track lives in a separate file next to the media rather than inside it.

fields.description:

fields.description:
The name the file gives the track, often a release tag: `VFF AC3 5.1 @448kb`. Empty
when the file writes an empty name, null when it writes none.

fields.name: streamIdentifier
fields.description:
The container's own number for the track: a Matroska track number, an MPEG-TS PID
(13 bits at most, so always within an `Int`).

fields.name: profile
fields.description:
The codec profile: `high` or `main 10` for video, `lc` for AAC, `ma` for DTS-HD
Master Audio, `dolby digital plus + dolby atmos`.

fields.name: bitDepth
fields.description: Bits per sample.

fields.name: requiredBandwidths
fields.description:
The bandwidth, in bits per second, the track needs to play without stalling, for each
of the buffer sizes the analysis tried, from the smallest: a larger buffer absorbs
more of the peaks. Empty when the track was never analysed that far.

Floats holding whole numbers: the analysis writes `2147483647` kilobits for a buffer
that no bandwidth fills, which in bits exceeds an `Int`.

fields.description: What the file says the track is for, beyond its language.

fields.description: What the analysis measured about a video track. Null on any other kind.

fields.name: audio

fields.name: subtitle

fields.description:

Bits per second as the file states them, else estimated, for a player budgeting its
bandwidth before reading anything: the header's rate, else the muxer's tagged one (not a
subtitle's), else a rate typical of an audio codec and its channels, and for a file's
one video what the container's declared rate leaves once every other track's is counted.

fields.name: startPlaybackSession
fields.description: Opens a playback session, or restarts the one already under this key.

args.name: input
args.description: The playback beginning.

fields.name: startStream
fields.description:
Starts sending a file to a player: as it is when the player reads it, its tracks
repackaged when they fit, the video re-encoded when they do not or a limit asks for it.
Records the playback session. A start under a key already streaming the same thing
keeps it running.

args.name: input
args.description: The stream to start.

fields.name: terminatePlaybackSession
fields.description:
Ends a session for an owner: its stream stops at once, and its player learns why from
`PlaybackSession.terminationReason`, listed under `playbackSessions(status: TERMINATED)`
until it stops. For the server's owners only.

args.name: input
args.description: The session to terminate.

fields.name: stopStream
fields.description: Stops a stream and closes its session.

args.name: input
args.description: The stream to stop.

fields.name: fallBackStream
fields.description:
Restarts a stream's conversion the more conservative way, under the same addresses, as a
player asks when it cannot decode what it receives: from hardware to software, from HEVC
to H.264. A sign of life for the session. This server's conversions all decode in
software and encode H.264 already, so a running one answers `NO_FALLBACK`.

args.name: input
args.description: The stream to restart.

fields.name: touchPlaybackSession
fields.description:
Records a sign of life, pushing the session's expiry forward and keeping its stream
running. Whether it is still playing: false once it has ended, expired or been
terminated.

args.name: key
args.description: The identifier the client chose for this playback.

fields.name: reportPlayback
fields.description:
Records where a player stands, pushing its sessions' expiry forward and keeping their
streams running, or ends them with their streams when it has stopped. Whether the
playback had any session playing, or any at all for a stop.

args.name: input
args.description: The player's report.

fields.name: chooseTracks
fields.description:
Chooses, for the caller, the audio track or the subtitle a file plays with — or no
subtitles. What is not named keeps its earlier choice. Returns the file.

args.name: file
args.description: The file, as returned in `MediaFile.id`.

args.name: audioTrack
args.description: One of the file's audio tracks, as returned in `MediaStream.id`.

args.name: subtitleTrack
args.description: One of the file's subtitles, as returned in `MediaStream.id`.

args.name: subtitlesOff
args.description: Play the file without subtitles, forced ones included.

fields.name: markWatched
fields.description:
Marks an item watched for the caller: a film or an episode once more, a season or a
series by each of its episodes once more. Counted on the episode's season and series
too. Returns the item's state after it.

args.name: id
args.description: The item, as returned in `id`.

fields.name: markUnwatched
fields.description:
Forgets what the caller watched of an item: an episode alone, a season with its
episodes, a series with its seasons and episodes. Returns the item's state after it.

args.name: id
args.description: The item, as returned in `id`.

fields.name: reportViewing
fields.description:
Records where a player stands in a playback. Past a minute and short of 90% of the
runtime the position is kept; crossing 90% within the playback counts a viewing and
forgets it.

args.name: input
args.description: The player's report.

fields.name: keepWatchPosition
fields.description:
Keeps a position for the caller without asking whether the item is finished: an
explicit "remember where I stopped". Under a minute, nothing is kept.

args.name: id
args.description: The item, as returned in `id`.

args.name: positionMs
args.description: Where to resume, in milliseconds.

fields.name: rateItem
fields.description:
Rates a film, a series, a season or an episode for the caller, or clears its rating.
The rating is the work's, shared by every copy of it, and nothing adds it up: a series
is rated on its own, whatever its episodes are.

args.name: input
args.description: The rating to give.

fields.name: setFavorite
fields.description:
Makes a film, a series, a season or an episode a favorite of the caller's, or takes it
back. The favorite is the work's: every copy of it is one.

args.name: input
args.description: The item and whether it is a favorite.

fields.name: setSubtitleOffset
fields.description:
Sets the offset the caller's player shifts a subtitle by, inside its media or a file
of its own. The offset is the caller's, on this one track.

args.name: input
args.description: The subtitle and its offset.

fields.name: deleteSidecar
fields.description:
Deletes a subtitle kept in a file of its own: the file, from disk when it is on this
machine where a sidecar of its media may be, and the track. For the library's admins
and the server's owners.

args.name: input
args.description: The subtitle to delete.

fields.name: scanLibrary
fields.description:
Starts scanning a library in the background: new files become items at once, and are
read afterwards, as are changed ones (`Library.analysis`); what is gone is removed —
unless its whole folder cannot be reached, which keeps it. For the library's admins and
the server's owners.

args.name: input
args.description: The library to scan.

fields.name: cancelLibraryScan
fields.description:
Asks a library's running scan to stop, and stops reading its files until its next
scan. What it already wrote stays.

args.name: input
args.description: The library whose scan to stop.

fields.name: readMediaFile
fields.description:
Reads a file's headers now when the server has not yet — its tracks, codecs and
durations, which a player needs before choosing how to play it — ahead of the files a
scan queued. Nothing to do for a file read already; `startStream` does it itself. For
whoever can see the file.

args.name: input
args.description: The file to read.

fields.name: deleteHistoryEntry
fields.description:
Deletes one viewing from a history: the caller's own, or anyone's for an owner.
What was watched stays as it is, as on the reference.

args.name: input
args.description: The entry to delete.

fields.name: createPlayQueue
fields.description:
Creates a play queue from a list of items, replacing the player's previous queue of
the same kind.

args.name: input
args.description: The queue to create.

fields.name: addToPlayQueue
fields.description: Queues items by hand in one of the caller's play queues.

args.name: input
args.description: The queue, the items and where they go.

fields.name: movePlayQueueEntry
fields.description: Moves one entry of one of the caller's play queues after another, or first.

args.name: input
args.description: The entry and where it goes.

fields.name: removeFromPlayQueue
fields.description: Takes one entry out of one of the caller's play queues.

args.name: input
args.description: The entry.

fields.name: clearPlayQueue
fields.description:
Removes every entry of one of the caller's play queues but the one playing, which ends
what was queued by hand.

args.name: input
args.description: The queue.

fields.name: resetPlayQueue
fields.description:
Makes the first entry of one of the caller's play queues the one playing. Leaves the
version as it is, as the reference does.

args.name: input
args.description: The queue.

fields.name: shufflePlayQueue
fields.description:
Rebuilds one of the caller's play queues from its source in random order, the entry
playing kept and first; every other entry is new. Refused while an entry queued by
hand remains.

args.name: input
args.description: The queue.

fields.name: unshufflePlayQueue
fields.description:
Rebuilds one of the caller's play queues from its source in natural order, the entry
playing kept where its item falls; every other entry is new. Refused while an entry
queued by hand remains.

args.name: input
args.description: The queue.

fields.name: endPlaybackSession
fields.description: Closes a session and stops its stream. Whether there was either.

args.name: key
args.description: The identifier the client chose for this playback.

fields.name: createUser
fields.description: Creates a user, active, with no password and no library. For the server's owners only.

args.name: input
args.description: The user's username, and its address if it has one.

fields.name: deleteUser
fields.description:
Deletes a user, its permissions and its connections. For the server's owners only; the
built-in `admin` account cannot be deleted.

args.name: input
args.description: The user to delete.

fields.name: setUserRole
fields.description:
Makes a user an owner of the server, or no longer one. For the server's owners only; the
built-in `admin` account cannot be demoted.

args.name: input
args.description: The user and its new role.

fields.name: setLibraryPermission
fields.description:
Gives a user a role on a library, replacing the one it had. For the server's owners
only.

args.name: input
args.description: The role to give.

fields.name: removeLibraryPermission
fields.description: Takes a library away from a user. Whether it had access. For the server's owners only.

args.name: userId
args.description: The user, as returned in `User.id`.

args.name: libraryId
args.description: The library, as returned in `Library.id`.

fields.name: disableExtension
fields.description:
Switches a user's connection off: its token stops working, its devices are forgotten
and its identifier is kept. Whether it was on. For the server's owners; through Jellyfin,
for the user itself too.

args.name: userId
args.description: The user, as returned in `User.id`.

args.name: extension
args.description: The protocol to disconnect.

fields.name: connectExtension
fields.description:
Connects a user through an extension, returning a new token. Called again, it replaces
the token and keeps the identifier clients recognize. For the server's owners; through
Jellyfin, whose clients then sign in with the user's password, for the user itself too.

args.name: userId
args.description: The user, as returned in `User.id`.

args.name: extension
args.description: The protocol to connect through.

fields.name: forgetExtensionDevice
fields.description:
Signs one device out of a user's connection: its token opens nothing more, and the
device signs in again with the password. Whether there was such a device. For the
server's owners, and for the user itself.

args.name: userId
args.description: The user, as returned in `User.id`.

args.name: extension
args.description: The protocol the device signed in through.

args.name: deviceId
args.description: The device, as returned in `ExtensionDevice.deviceId`.

fields.name: signInWithTicket
fields.description:
Signs a browser in with a one-time ticket, as `signIn` does with a password: the server
hands such a ticket out only in an address it opens itself (its tray icon on Windows).
A ticket works once, for a minute.

args.name: input
args.description: The ticket the address carried.

fields.name: setPassword
fields.description:
Gives the caller a new password, which also signs it in through Jellyfin's clients; its
current password is asked for when it has one. An owner sets or resets any user's,
with none asked. The built-in `admin` account takes `KLAPZ_ADMIN_PASSWORD` again at the
next start when that is set.

args.name: input
args.description: The current password, and the new one.

fields.name: pairExtension
fields.description:
Ties a user's connection to its account on the extension's own service, and tells that
service where the server can be reached. For the server's owners, and for the user
itself.

args.name: input
args.description: The account's pairing code, and where to reach the server.

fields.name: moveExtension
fields.description:
Changes where a paired server is reached, and tells the extension's service at once:
what a tunnel or a new domain needs, without pairing again. For the server's owners,
and for the user itself.

args.name: input
args.description: The paired connection, and its new address.

fields.name: unpairExtension
fields.description:
Forgets the account tied to a user's connection. Whether there was one. For the server's
owners, and for the user itself.

args.name: userId
args.description: The user, as returned in `User.id`.

args.name: extension
args.description: The protocol to unpair.

fields.name: signUp
fields.description:
Creates an account that signs in with a password. It waits, inactive, until an owner
lets it in. Open to anyone.

args.name: input
args.description: The username, address and password of the new account.

fields.name: signIn
fields.description:
Checks a username or an address and its password and, when they match an active user,
opens a session for it: a cookie the server reads on every request, whose value a
client that is no browser can present as `Authorization: Bearer`. Open to anyone;
failed attempts on one username or address are limited.

args.name: input
args.description: The username or address, and the password, to sign in with.

fields.name: signOut
fields.description: Clears the session cookie.

fields.name: signInThroughExtension
fields.description:
Checks a username or an address and its password, as `signIn` does, for a client of an
extension whose clients sign in with a password — Jellyfin's — and gives the client's
device a token of its own. The user must be connected through the extension, and its
connection on. Open to anyone; failed attempts count with `signIn`'s.

args.name: input
args.description: The extension, the credentials and the device signing in.

fields.name: signOutOfExtension
fields.description:
Signs a device out of an extension: its token opens nothing more. Only the caller's own
devices; whether the token was one.

args.name: extension
args.description: The protocol the token was issued for.

args.name: token
args.description: The token the device was given.

fields.name: activateUser
fields.description: Lets in a user who signed up, or one that was shut out. For the server's owners only.

args.name: input
args.description: The user to let in.

fields.name: deactivateUser
fields.description:
Shuts a user out: its sessions and its tokens stop opening anything at once, and it
keeps its libraries for when it is let in again. For the server's owners only; the
built-in `admin` account cannot be shut out.

args.name: input
args.description: The user to shut out.

fields.name: matchItem
fields.description:
Matches a film or a series to a record of its library's provider — the one named, else
the one it shows already, else the best search result — and fetches its metadata and
images in the background. For a library's admins and the server's owners.

args.name: input
args.description: The item and the record.

fields.name: refreshItemMetadata
fields.description:
Fetches a film's or a series' metadata and images again from the record it shows, in
the background; one never matched is searched for. For a library's admins and the
server's owners.

args.name: input
args.description: The item.

fields.name: unmatchItem
fields.description:
Forgets the record a film or a series and its seasons and episodes show: they take back
the identity a scan gives, and keep their texts until matched again. For a library's
admins and the server's owners.

args.name: input
args.description: The item.

fields.name: updateMovie
fields.description: Changes a film's metadata and locks. For a library's admins and the server's owners.

args.name: input
args.description: The changes.

fields.name: updateShow
fields.description: Changes a series' metadata and locks. For a library's admins and the server's owners.

args.name: input
args.description: The changes.

fields.name: updateEpisode
fields.description: Changes an episode's metadata and locks. For a library's admins and the server's owners.

args.name: input
args.description: The changes.

fields.name: addMarker
fields.description:
Adds a marker to a film or an episode: an intro, credits or a commercial, for its
library's admins and the server's owners, or a bookmark of the caller's own.

args.name: input
args.description: The marker to add.

fields.name: updateMarker
fields.description:
Moves a marker or changes what it says. The work's markers for its library's admins
and the server's owners, a bookmark for its owner.

args.name: input
args.description: The changes.

fields.name: deleteMarker
fields.description:
Removes a marker. The work's markers for its library's admins and the server's owners, a
bookmark for its owner.

args.name: input
args.description: The marker to remove.

fields.name: createPlaylist
fields.description: Creates a playlist of the caller's: of chosen items, or smart with a rule.

args.name: input
args.description: The playlist to create.

fields.name: updatePlaylist
fields.description: Renames, describes, locks or unlocks one of the caller's playlists.

args.name: input
args.description: The changes.

fields.name: deletePlaylist
fields.description: Deletes one of the caller's playlists, and its entries with it.

args.name: input
args.description: The playlist to delete.

fields.name: addToPlaylist
fields.description: Appends items to one of the caller's playlists of chosen items, skipping those it holds.

args.name: input
args.description: The playlist and the items.

fields.name: removeFromPlaylist
fields.description: Takes one entry out of one of the caller's playlists.

args.name: input
args.description: The entry.

fields.name: movePlaylistEntry
fields.description: Moves one entry of one of the caller's playlists after another, or first.

args.name: input
args.description: The entry and where it goes.

fields.name: clearPlaylist
fields.description: Empties one of the caller's playlists of chosen items.

args.name: input
args.description: The playlist to empty.

fields.name: createLibrary
fields.description:
Creates a library over directories of the server, then scans it. For the server's
owners only.

args.name: input
args.description: The library to create.

fields.name: updateLibrary
fields.description:
Renames a library or changes its language, for its admins and the server's owners;
changes the directories it scans, for the owners only.

args.name: input
args.description: The changes.

fields.name: deleteLibrary
fields.description:
Deletes a library with its items, collections and the permissions given on it, ending
every playback of its items; its files stay on disk, and watch state and ratings stay
with the works. For the server's owners only.

args.name: input
args.description: The library to delete.

fields.name: createCollection
fields.description:
Creates a collection in a library: of chosen items, or smart with a rule. For the
library's admins and the server's owners.

args.name: input
args.description: The collection to create.

fields.name: updateCollection
fields.description:
Renames, describes, sets, locks or unlocks a collection. For its library's admins and
the server's owners.

args.name: input
args.description: The changes.

fields.name: deleteCollection
fields.description:
Deletes a collection; its items stay in the library. For its library's admins and the
server's owners.

args.name: input
args.description: The collection to delete.

fields.name: addToCollection
fields.description:
Adds items to a collection of chosen items, skipping those it holds. For its library's
admins and the server's owners.

args.name: input
args.description: The collection and the items.

fields.name: removeFromCollection
fields.description:
Takes an item out of a collection of chosen items. For its library's admins and the
server's owners.

args.name: input
args.description: The collection and the item.

fields.name: moveCollectionItem
fields.description:
Moves an item of a collection after another, or first, in its custom order. For its
library's admins and the server's owners.

args.name: input
args.description: The item and where it goes.

fields.name: clearCollection
fields.description:
Takes every item out of a collection of chosen items, keeping the collection. For its
library's admins and the server's owners.

args.name: input
args.description: The collection to empty.

fields.name: replacePlaylistRule
fields.description: Replaces the rule of one of the caller's smart playlists.

args.name: input
args.description: The playlist and its new rule.

types.description:
Object and Interface types are described by a list of Fields, each of which
has a name, potentially a list of arguments, and a return type.

types.name: __InputValue
types.description:
Arguments provided to Fields or Directives and the input fields of an
InputObject are represented as Input Values which describe their type and
optionally a default value.

types.name: __Schema
types.description:
A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes
all available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry
points for query, mutation, and subscription operations.

fields.name: description
fields.description:
description of __Schema for newer graphiql introspection schema
requirements

fields.name: types
fields.description: A list of all types supported by this server.

fields.name: queryType
fields.description: The type that query operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: mutationType
fields.description:
If this server supports mutation, the type that mutation operations will
be rooted at.

fields.name: subscriptionType
fields.description:
If this server support subscription, the type that subscription
operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: directives
fields.description: A list of all directives supported by this server.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds
of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about
that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name and
description, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface
types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface,
provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose
other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description:
Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid
fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description:
Indicates this type is an interface. `fields` and `possibleTypes` are
valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.
